newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kombat seen in full production by April.
newsitem.headline: Kombat seen in full production by April.

text.p: Gold Fields of Namibia Ltd said on Monday that its Kombat copper mine was likely to be in full production by April, after operations were suspended on January 7 when the mine flooded.
Flooding followed a breakthrough of fissure water in a development drive some 300 metres below the surface.
Kombat is one of three mines operated by Gold Fields Namibia subsidiary Tsumeb Corp Ltd.
Two concrete water sealing plugs in the immediate vicinity of the water inflow were installed by January 20 and the inflow sealed off.
"Dewatering of the mine has progressed well," Gold Fields said. It said that pumping had been recommissioned and dewatering would proceed at an increased rate.
"Rock hoisting is now possible from 14 level and production at 1 shaft will now recommence," Gold Fields said.
The company said that since January 28, the loss of production had been partly offset by mining at Kombat 3 shaft and by increased production from the Khusib Springs mine.
